questions.q: Why does the lab tag resources with team, environment, and cost-center before building the cost view?
options: Tags are required by Azure before any resource can run
A cost grouping by tag is only as good as tagging coverage -- untagged resources show up as a blind 'Untagged' bucket on every chart
Tags automatically reduce the cloud bill
Tags replace the need for a budget entirely
questions.explain: Incomplete tag coverage creates an Untagged bucket on every grouped chart -- exactly the blind spot that let an unexplained spike go unnoticed before this lab.

questions.q: What does grouping the cost analysis view by tag: team actually answer that a flat resource list can't?
options: Who is spending -- which team's resources are driving cost, instead of an unattributed list of VM and storage names
The exact CPU utilization of every VM
Whether a resource is tagged correctly
How many Kubernetes pods are running
questions.explain: Grouping by team turns a flat, unattributable resource list into a view that directly answers who is responsible for which spend.

questions.q: Why does the lab pin the cost view onto the same dashboard as the Chapter 4 reliability panels, instead of leaving it inside Cost Management alone?
options: Cost Management cannot display charts on its own
Pinned dashboards are cheaper to run than Cost Management
So the people who make a cost-cutting change see its cost and its reliability blast radius in the same place every day
Because Grafana requires all data to come from one source
questions.explain: Keeping cost and reliability visibility separate is exactly the gap that lets a cost-cutting decision go unexamined for its reliability impact -- the scenario Lesson 31 walks through.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between the budget's Actual_80 threshold and its Forecasted_100 threshold?
options: They are functionally identical
Actual_80 only applies to dev environments
Forecasted_100 only triggers after the month has already ended
Actual_80 warns at 80% of real spend already incurred; Forecasted_100 warns when the month is projected to exceed budget before it actually does, giving more lead time
questions.explain: Staging an actual threshold with a forecasted threshold gives the team warning while spend is still projected, not only after real money has already been spent.

questions.q: How does an anomaly alert differ from the staged budget alerts configured earlier in the lab?
options: An anomaly alert fires relative to the resource's own recent spending pattern, catching a spike days before a fixed monthly budget threshold would ever cross
Anomaly alerts and budget alerts are the same feature under two names
Anomaly alerts only work for compute resources, never storage
Anomaly alerts replace the need for tagging
questions.explain: A budget alert compares spend to a fixed monthly number; an anomaly alert compares spend to the account's own recent pattern, which is what catches a spike early instead of at month's end.
